```{r}
# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Set up a 1x2 plotting area to match the whiteboard's two graphs
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))

# =====================================================================
# 1. MCMC (Markov Chain Monte Carlo) Example
# Demonstrating sampling from a complex (multimodal) target distribution
# =====================================================================

# Define a complex target density (e.g., a mixture of two normals)
target_density <- function(x) {
  0.4 * dnorm(x, mean = -2, sd = 1) + 0.6 * dnorm(x, mean = 2, sd = 1.5)
}

# Metropolis-Hastings MCMC Algorithm
n_iter <- 10000
samples_mcmc <- numeric(n_iter)
current_x <- 0 # Initial value

for (i in 1:n_iter) {
  # Propose a new state from a Normal distribution centered at current state
  proposed_x <- rnorm(1, mean = current_x, sd = 1)
  
  # Calculate acceptance ratio
  acceptance_ratio <- target_density(proposed_x) / target_density(current_x)
  
  # Accept or reject
  if (runif(1) < acceptance_ratio) {
    current_x <- proposed_x
  }
  samples_mcmc[i] <- current_x
}

# Plot MCMC results (Histogram with overlaid density line, like the whiteboard)
hist(samples_mcmc, breaks = 40, freq = FALSE, col = "lightblue", 
     main = "MCMC Sampling (Complex Posterior)", xlab = expression(theta),
     border = "white")
# Overlay the true target density line
curve(target_density(x), add = TRUE, col = "darkblue", lwd = 2)


# =====================================================================
# 2. MC (Monte Carlo) Example
# Demonstrating direct sampling from a known, closed-form distribution
# =====================================================================

# Direct Monte Carlo sampling using built-in standard distribution functions
mu <- 0
sigma <- 1
samples_mc <- rnorm(10000, mean = mu, sd = sigma)

# Plot MC results (Simple bell curve, like the right side of the whiteboard)
hist(samples_mc, breaks = 40, freq = FALSE, col = "lightgreen", 
     main = "MC Sampling (Known Form)", xlab = expression(theta),
     border = "white")
# Overlay the theoretical normal density line
curve(dnorm(x, mean = mu, sd = sigma), add = TRUE, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2)

# Reset plotting parameters
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r}
# Set seed so you get the exact same visual result if you run this
set.seed(123)

# Total number of steps the chain will take
n_iter <- 2000

# Initialize a vector to store our MCMC samples
samples <- numeric(n_iter)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE SETUP
# Let's say our true posterior distribution is centered at 10.
# We are going to start our chain FAR AWAY at -50 to force it to 
# search for the stationary distribution (the burn-in phase).
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
current_x <- -50 
samples[1] <- current_x

# Define our target posterior distribution (Normal with mean=10, sd=2)
target_density <- function(x) {
  dnorm(x, mean = 10, sd = 2)
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE MCMC ALGORITHM (Metropolis-Hastings)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
for (i in 2:n_iter) {
  # Propose a new step (random walk around the current position)
  proposed_x <- rnorm(1, mean = current_x, sd = 3)
  
  # Calculate acceptance ratio (Posterior of Proposal / Posterior of Current)
  ratio <- target_density(proposed_x) / target_density(current_x)
  
  # Accept or reject the proposal
  if (runif(1) < ratio) {
    current_x <- proposed_x
  }
  
  # Log the sample
  samples[i] <- current_x
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# VISUALIZATION
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Set up a 2x1 plot area
par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

# Plot 1: The Trace Plot (Showing the "finding" phase and the "stationary" phase)
plot(1:n_iter, samples, type = "l", col = "steelblue", 
     main = "Trace Plot: Notice the 'Burn-in' oscillation at the start",
     xlab = "Iteration Number", ylab = "Parameter Value")

# Add a line for where the true posterior is located
abline(h = 10, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2) 

# Add a line indicating where the chain seems to have found the stationary distribution
abline(v = 150, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2, lty = 2) 
legend("bottomright", legend = c("MCMC Chain", "True Mean (Posterior)", "End of Burn-in"), 
       col = c("steelblue", "red", "darkgreen"), lty = c(1, 2, 2))

# Plot 2: Histogram of the samples AFTER discarding the initial oscillation
burn_in_period <- 150
valid_samples <- samples[(burn_in_period + 1):n_iter]

hist(valid_samples, breaks = 30, freq = FALSE, col = "lightblue", border = "white",
     main = "Stationary Distribution (Posterior) After Burn-in",
     xlab = "Parameter Value")

# Overlay the true posterior curve to show they match
curve(dnorm(x, mean = 10, sd = 2), add = TRUE, col = "darkred", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("Sampled Posterior", "True Posterior Density"), 
       fill = c("lightblue", NA), border = c("white", NA), 
       col = c(NA, "darkred"), lwd = c(NA, 2))

# Reset plot settings
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

### The 5-Step ABC Algorithm Loop

```{r}
# Clear workspace and set seed
rm(list = ls())
set.seed(123)

# =====================================================================
# 1. SETUP MODEL PARAMETERS & OBSERVED DATA (X)
# =====================================================================

n <- 50             # Sample size
true_mu <- 3        # True parameter value
data_sd <- 1        # Known SD

# Prior setup: theta (mu) ~ N(mu_0, sigma_0^2)
mu_0 <- 0           
sigma_0 <- 2        

# Observed Dataset: X = (x_1, ..., x_n)
X_obs <- rnorm(n, mean = true_mu, sd = data_sd)

# Analytical True Posterior
post_var  <- 1 / (1 / sigma_0^2 + n / data_sd^2)
post_sd   <- sqrt(post_var)
post_mean <- post_var * (mu_0 / sigma_0^2 + sum(X_obs) / data_sd^2)


# =====================================================================
# 2. ABC ALGORITHM FUNCTION
# =====================================================================

run_abc <- function(X_obs, summary_func, epsilon = 0.05, n_sim = 100000) {
  # Calculate summary statistic for observed data X
  X_stat_obs <- summary_func(X_obs)
  
  # Vectors to store tracking metrics
  accepted_theta_star <- numeric()
  accepted_Y_stat     <- numeric()
  accepted_distances  <- numeric()
  
  for (i in 1:n_sim) {
    # Step 1: Draw proposal theta* ~ Prior
    theta_star <- rnorm(1, mean = mu_0, sd = sigma_0)
    
    # Step 2: Simulate dataset Y ~ Model(theta*)
    Y_sim <- rnorm(n, mean = theta_star, sd = data_sd)
    
    # Step 3: Compute summary statistic for simulated data Y
    Y_stat_sim <- summary_func(Y_sim)
    
    # Step 4: Distance d(Y_stat, X_stat)
    distance <- abs(Y_stat_sim - X_stat_obs)
    
    # Step 5: Accept if distance < epsilon
    if (distance < epsilon) {
      accepted_theta_star <- c(accepted_theta_star, theta_star)
      accepted_Y_stat     <- c(accepted_Y_stat, Y_stat_sim)
      accepted_distances  <- c(accepted_distances, distance)
    }
  }
  
  return(list(
    theta_star_vals = accepted_theta_star,
    Y_stat_vals     = accepted_Y_stat,
    distances       = accepted_distances,
    X_stat_obs      = X_stat_obs,
    total_sims      = n_sim
  ))
}


# =====================================================================
# 3. RUN EXPERIMENTS FOR ALL 3 SUMMARY STATISTICS
# =====================================================================

epsilon <- 0.05 
n_simulations <- 100000

cat("Running ABC simulations...\n")

# Choice 1: Sample Mean (X_bar vs Y_bar)
abc_mean <- run_abc(X_obs, summary_func = mean, epsilon = epsilon, n_sim = n_simulations)

# Choice 2: Sample Median (Median(X) vs Median(Y))
abc_median <- run_abc(X_obs, summary_func = median, epsilon = epsilon, n_sim = n_simulations)

# Choice 3: First Observation (X_1 vs Y_1)
abc_first <- run_abc(X_obs, summary_func = function(x) x[1], epsilon = epsilon, n_sim = n_simulations)


# =====================================================================
# 4. VISUALIZATION & LAYOUT
# =====================================================================

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 4.5, 5, 2))

# --- Plot 1: Sample Mean ---
dens_mean <- density(abc_mean$theta_star_vals)
plot(dens_mean, col = "darkblue", lwd = 2, 
     main = "ABC with Sample Mean\nSufficient Statistics", 
     cex.main = 0.95,
     xlab = expression(mu), ylab = "Density", xlim = c(1, 5),
     ylim = c(0, max(dens_mean$y, dnorm(post_mean, post_mean, post_sd)) * 1.1))

curve(dnorm(x, mean = post_mean, sd = post_sd), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("ABC (Sample Mean)", "True Posterior"),
       col = c("darkblue", "red"), lty = c(1, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n")

# --- Plot 2: Comparing All 3 Statistics ---
plot(density(abc_mean$theta_star_vals), col = "darkblue", lwd = 2, 
     main = "Impact of Different\nSummary Statistics", 
     cex.main = 0.95,
     xlab = expression(mu), ylab = "Density", xlim = c(-1, 6),
     ylim = c(0, max(dens_mean$y) * 1.1))

lines(density(abc_median$theta_star_vals), col = "forestgreen", lwd = 2)
lines(density(abc_first$theta_star_vals), col = "orange", lwd = 2)
curve(dnorm(x, mean = post_mean, sd = post_sd), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)

legend("topleft", 
       legend = c(as.expression(bquote("Mean (Suff: " ~ bar(X) ~ ", " ~ bar(Y) ~ ")")), 
                  "Median (Median(X), Median(Y))", 
                  expression("First Obs (" ~ X[1] ~ ", " ~ Y[1] ~ ")"), 
                  "True Posterior"),
       col = c("darkblue", "forestgreen", "orange", "red"), 
       lty = c(1, 1, 1, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.75)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))


# =====================================================================
# 5. PRINT DETAILED RESULTS FOR ALL THREE STATISTICS
# =====================================================================

print_full_metrics <- function(abc_list, model_name, x_symbol, y_symbol) {
  acc_count <- length(abc_list$theta_star_vals)
  acc_rate  <- (acc_count / abc_list$total_sims) * 100
  
  cat(sprintf("\n--- %s ---\n", model_name))
  cat("Accepted Count                :", acc_count, sprintf("(Acceptance Rate: %.2f%%)\n", acc_rate))
  cat(sprintf("Observed Statistic (%s)      : %.4f\n", x_symbol, abc_list$X_stat_obs))
  cat(sprintf("Mean Simulated Statistic (%s): %.4f\n", y_symbol, mean(abc_list$Y_stat_vals)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean Distance |%s - %s|      : %.4f\n", y_symbol, x_symbol, mean(abc_list$distances)))
  cat(sprintf("Max Distance (Must be < eps)  : %.4f\n", max(abc_list$distances)))
  cat("Estimated Posterior Mean (mu)  :", round(mean(abc_list$theta_star_vals), 4), "\n")
  cat("Estimated Posterior SD (mu)    :", round(sd(abc_list$theta_star_vals), 4), "\n")
}

cat("\n===================================================\n")
cat("            ABC FULL SIMULATION RESULTS            \n")
cat("===================================================\n")
cat("True Analytical Posterior Mean:", round(post_mean, 4), "\n")
cat("True Analytical Posterior SD  :", round(post_sd, 4), "\n")
cat("Epsilon Tolerance (epsilon)   :", epsilon, "\n")

# Print details for Choice 1
print_full_metrics(abc_mean, "1. SAMPLE MEAN", "X_bar", "Y_bar")

# Print details for Choice 2
print_full_metrics(abc_median, "2. SAMPLE MEDIAN", "Median(X)", "Median(Y)")

# Print details for Choice 3
print_full_metrics(abc_first, "3. FIRST OBSERVATION", "X_1", "Y_1")

cat("\n===================================================\n")
```

```{r}
# Clear workspace and set seed
rm(list = ls())
set.seed(123)

# =====================================================================
# 1. SETUP MODEL PARAMETERS & OBSERVED DATA (X)
# =====================================================================

n <- 50             # Sample size
true_mu <- 3        # True parameter value
data_sd <- 1        # Known SD

# Prior setup: theta (mu) ~ N(mu_0, sigma_0^2)
mu_0 <- 0           
sigma_0 <- 2        

# Observed Dataset: X = (x_1, ..., x_n)
X_obs <- rnorm(n, mean = true_mu, sd = data_sd)

# Analytical True Posterior
post_var  <- 1 / (1 / sigma_0^2 + n / data_sd^2)
post_sd   <- sqrt(post_var)
post_mean <- post_var * (mu_0 / sigma_0^2 + sum(X_obs) / data_sd^2)


# =====================================================================
# 2. ABC ALGORITHM FUNCTION
# =====================================================================

run_abc <- function(X_obs, summary_func, epsilon, n_sim = 100000) {
  X_stat_obs <- summary_func(X_obs)
  
  accepted_theta_star <- numeric()
  accepted_Y_stat     <- numeric()
  accepted_distances  <- numeric()
  
  for (i in 1:n_sim) {
    # Step 1: Draw proposal theta* ~ Prior
    theta_star <- rnorm(1, mean = mu_0, sd = sigma_0)
    
    # Step 2: Simulate dataset Y ~ Model(theta*)
    Y_sim <- rnorm(n, mean = theta_star, sd = data_sd)
    
    # Step 3: Compute summary statistic
    Y_stat_sim <- summary_func(Y_sim)
    
    # Step 4: Distance d(Y_stat, X_stat)
    distance <- abs(Y_stat_sim - X_stat_obs)
    
    # Step 5: Accept if distance < epsilon
    if (distance < epsilon) {
      accepted_theta_star <- c(accepted_theta_star, theta_star)
      accepted_Y_stat     <- c(accepted_Y_stat, Y_stat_sim)
      accepted_distances  <- c(accepted_distances, distance)
    }
  }
  
  return(list(
    theta_star_vals = accepted_theta_star,
    Y_stat_vals     = accepted_Y_stat,
    distances       = accepted_distances,
    X_stat_obs      = X_stat_obs,
    total_sims      = n_sim,
    epsilon         = epsilon
  ))
}


# =====================================================================
# 3. RUN EXPERIMENTS ACROSS DIFFERENT EPSILON VALUES
# =====================================================================

eps_list <- c(0.5, 0.1, 0.05, 0.01)
n_simulations <- 100000
results <- list()

cat("Running ABC simulations across different epsilon values...\n")

for (eps in eps_list) {
  cat(sprintf("Simulating for epsilon = %.2f...\n", eps))
  results[[as.character(eps)]] <- run_abc(
    X_obs = X_obs, 
    summary_func = mean, 
    epsilon = eps, 
    n_sim = n_simulations
  )
}


# =====================================================================
# 4. VISUALIZATION & LAYOUT
# =====================================================================

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 4.5, 4, 2))

# Color palette for epsilons
colors <- c("purple", "forestgreen", "darkblue", "orange")

# --- Plot 1: Density Comparisons across Epsilon ---
# Calculate density for smallest epsilon to gauge y-limit
dens_tight <- density(results[["0.01"]]$theta_star_vals)
max_y <- max(dens_tight$y, dnorm(post_mean, post_mean, post_sd)) * 1.15

plot(dens_tight, col = colors[4], lwd = 2, 
     main = expression(paste("Impact of Tolerance Threshold (", epsilon, ")")),
     cex.main = 0.95,
     xlab = expression(mu), ylab = "Density", xlim = c(1, 5), ylim = c(0, max_y))

for (k in 1:(length(eps_list) - 1)) {
  eps_str <- as.character(eps_list[k])
  lines(density(results[[eps_str]]$theta_star_vals), col = colors[k], lwd = 2)
}

# Add True Posterior
curve(dnorm(x, mean = post_mean, sd = post_sd), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)

legend("topleft", 
       legend = c(paste("eps =", eps_list), "True Posterior"),
       col = c(colors, "red"), 
       lty = c(rep(1, length(eps_list)), 2), 
       lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)

# --- Plot 2: Acceptance Rate vs. Epsilon Trade-off ---
acc_rates <- sapply(results, function(res) (length(res$theta_star_vals) / res$total_sims) * 100)

plot(eps_list, acc_rates, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "darkblue", lwd = 2,
     main = expression(paste("Acceptance Rate vs. Tolerance (", epsilon, ")")),
     cex.main = 0.95,
     xlab = expression(epsilon), ylab = "Acceptance Rate (%)",
     log = "x") # log scale highlights the dramatic drop at tiny epsilons

grid()

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))


# =====================================================================
# 5. PRINT DETAILED RESULTS TABLE
# =====================================================================

cat("\n=================================================================================\n")
cat("                     ABC TOLERANCE (EPSILON) EXPERIMENT RESULTS                 \n")
cat("=================================================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Analytical True Posterior Mean: %.4f | SD: %.4f\n", post_mean, post_sd))
cat("---------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n")

# Header
cat(sprintf("%-10s | %-12s | %-12s | %-15s | %-15s\n", 
            "Epsilon", "Accepted N", "Accept Rate", "Post Mean (mu)", "Post SD (mu)"))
cat("---------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n")

for (eps in eps_list) {
  res <- results[[as.character(eps)]]
  acc_count <- length(res$theta_star_vals)
  acc_rate  <- (acc_count / res$total_sims) * 100
  p_mean    <- mean(res$theta_star_vals)
  p_sd      <- sd(res$theta_star_vals)
  
  cat(sprintf("%-10.2f | %-12d | %-11.2f%% | %-15.4f | %-15.4f\n", 
              eps, acc_count, acc_rate, p_mean, p_sd))
}

cat("=================================================================================\n")
```

```{r}
# Clear workspace and set seed
rm(list = ls())
set.seed(123)

# =====================================================================
# 1. SETUP MODEL PARAMETERS & OBSERVED DATA (X)
# =====================================================================

n <- 50             # Sample size
true_mu <- 3        # True parameter value
data_sd <- 1        # Known SD

# Prior setup: theta (mu) ~ N(mu_0, sigma_0^2)
mu_0 <- 0           
sigma_0 <- 2        

# Observed Dataset: X = (x_1, ..., x_n)
X_obs <- rnorm(n, mean = true_mu, sd = data_sd)

# Analytical True Posterior
post_var  <- 1 / (1 / sigma_0^2 + n / data_sd^2)
post_sd   <- sqrt(post_var)
post_mean <- post_var * (mu_0 / sigma_0^2 + sum(X_obs) / data_sd^2)


# =====================================================================
# 2. JOINT SUMMARY STATISTIC & COVARIANCE ESTIMATION (PILOT RUN)
# =====================================================================

# Multi-dimensional summary statistic: Joint Sample Mean & Sample Median
summary_func <- function(x) c(mean = mean(x), median = median(x))
X_stat_obs <- summary_func(X_obs)

# Pilot simulation to estimate scale/covariance matrix for Weighted & Mahalanobis metrics
n_pilot <- 2000
pilot_stats <- t(sapply(1:n_pilot, function(i) {
  theta_p <- rnorm(1, mean = mu_0, sd = sigma_0)
  summary_func(rnorm(n, mean = theta_p, sd = data_sd))
}))

cov_matrix  <- cov(pilot_stats)      # Full covariance matrix (for Mahalanobis)
cov_inv     <- solve(cov_matrix)     # Inverse covariance
var_weights <- diag(cov_matrix)      # Variance weights (for Weighted Euclidean)


# =====================================================================
# 3. ABC ALGORITHM FUNCTION (DISTANCE METRIC VARIATIONS)
# =====================================================================

run_abc_dist <- function(X_obs, summary_func, dist_metric = "euclidean", epsilon = 0.05, n_sim = 100000) {
  
  X_stat_obs <- summary_func(X_obs)
  
  accepted_theta_star <- numeric()
  accepted_Y_stat     <- list()
  accepted_distances  <- numeric()
  
  for (i in 1:n_sim) {
    # Step 1: Draw proposal theta* ~ Prior
    theta_star <- rnorm(1, mean = mu_0, sd = sigma_0)
    
    # Step 2: Simulate dataset Y ~ Model(theta*)
    Y_sim <- rnorm(n, mean = theta_star, sd = data_sd)
    
    # Step 3: Compute summary statistic vector for simulated data Y
    Y_stat_sim <- summary_func(Y_sim)
    diff <- Y_stat_sim - X_stat_obs
    
    # Step 4: Distance metric d(Y_stat, X_stat)
    if (dist_metric == "euclidean") {
      # Standard Euclidean Distance (Identity matrix)
      distance <- sqrt(sum(diff^2))
    } else if (dist_metric == "weighted") {
      # Weighted Euclidean Distance (Diagonal variance matrix)
      distance <- sqrt(sum((diff^2) / var_weights))
    } else if (dist_metric == "mahalanobis") {
      # Mahalanobis Distance (Full covariance matrix)
      distance <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(diff) %*% cov_inv %*% diff))
    }
    
    # Step 5: Accept if distance < epsilon
    if (distance < epsilon) {
      accepted_theta_star <- c(accepted_theta_star, theta_star)
      accepted_Y_stat[[length(accepted_Y_stat) + 1]] <- Y_stat_sim
      accepted_distances  <- c(accepted_distances, distance)
    }
  }
  
  Y_stat_mat <- do.call(rbind, accepted_Y_stat)
  
  return(list(
    theta_star_vals = accepted_theta_star,
    Y_stat_vals     = Y_stat_mat,
    distances       = accepted_distances,
    X_stat_obs      = X_stat_obs,
    total_sims      = n_sim
  ))
}


# =====================================================================
# 4. RUN EXPERIMENTS FOR ALL 3 DISTANCE METRICS
# =====================================================================

epsilon <- 0.05 
n_simulations <- 100000

cat("Running ABC simulations across distance metrics...\n")

# Choice 1: Standard Euclidean Distance
abc_euclidean <- run_abc_dist(X_obs, summary_func, dist_metric = "euclidean", epsilon = epsilon, n_sim = n_simulations)

# Choice 2: Weighted Euclidean Distance
abc_weighted <- run_abc_dist(X_obs, summary_func, dist_metric = "weighted", epsilon = epsilon, n_sim = n_simulations)

# Choice 3: Mahalanobis Distance
abc_mahalanobis <- run_abc_dist(X_obs, summary_func, dist_metric = "mahalanobis", epsilon = epsilon, n_sim = n_simulations)


# =====================================================================
# 5. VISUALIZATION & LAYOUT (2x2 GRID WITH CORNER-ALIGNED LEGENDS)
# =====================================================================

par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3.5, 2))

# Compute maximum height and add headroom (35%) to avoid legend overlap
max_y <- max(
  density(abc_euclidean$theta_star_vals)$y,
  density(abc_weighted$theta_star_vals)$y,
  density(abc_mahalanobis$theta_star_vals)$y,
  dnorm(post_mean, post_mean, post_sd)
) * 1.35

# --- Plot 1: Standard Euclidean Distance ---
dens_euc <- density(abc_euclidean$theta_star_vals)
plot(dens_euc, col = "darkblue", lwd = 2, 
     main = "ABC with Standard Euclidean\nJoint (Mean, Median)", 
     cex.main = 0.95,
     xlab = expression(mu), ylab = "Density", xlim = c(0.5, 5.5),
     ylim = c(0, max_y))

curve(dnorm(x, mean = post_mean, sd = post_sd), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topleft", legend = c("ABC (Euclidean)", "True Posterior"),
       col = c("darkblue", "red"), lty = c(1, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.75)

# --- Plot 2: Weighted Euclidean Distance ---
dens_weight <- density(abc_weighted$theta_star_vals)
plot(dens_weight, col = "forestgreen", lwd = 2, 
     main = "ABC with Weighted Euclidean\nJoint (Mean, Median)", 
     cex.main = 0.95,
     xlab = expression(mu), ylab = "Density", xlim = c(0.5, 5.5),
     ylim = c(0, max_y))

curve(dnorm(x, mean = post_mean, sd = post_sd), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topleft", legend = c("ABC (Weighted)", "True Posterior"),
       col = c("forestgreen", "red"), lty = c(1, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.75)

# --- Plot 3: Mahalanobis Distance ---
dens_mahal <- density(abc_mahalanobis$theta_star_vals)
plot(dens_mahal, col = "purple", lwd = 2, 
     main = "ABC with Mahalanobis Distance\nJoint (Mean, Median)", 
     cex.main = 0.95,
     xlab = expression(mu), ylab = "Density", xlim = c(0.5, 5.5),
     ylim = c(0, max_y))

curve(dnorm(x, mean = post_mean, sd = post_sd), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topleft", legend = c("ABC (Mahalanobis)", "True Posterior"),
       col = c("purple", "red"), lty = c(1, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.75)

# --- Plot 4: Comparing All 3 Distance Metrics ---
plot(density(abc_euclidean$theta_star_vals), col = "darkblue", lwd = 2, 
     main = "Impact of Different\nDistance Metrics", 
     cex.main = 0.95,
     xlab = expression(mu), ylab = "Density", xlim = c(0.5, 5.5),
     ylim = c(0, max_y))

lines(density(abc_weighted$theta_star_vals), col = "forestgreen", lwd = 2)
lines(density(abc_mahalanobis$theta_star_vals), col = "purple", lwd = 2)
curve(dnorm(x, mean = post_mean, sd = post_sd), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)

legend("topleft", 
       legend = c("Standard Euclidean", 
                  "Weighted Euclidean", 
                  "Mahalanobis Distance", 
                  "True Posterior"),
       col = c("darkblue", "forestgreen", "purple", "red"), 
       lty = c(1, 1, 1, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.70)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))


# =====================================================================
# 6. PRINT DETAILED RESULTS FOR ALL THREE DISTANCE METRICS
# =====================================================================

print_full_metrics <- function(abc_list, model_name) {
  acc_count <- length(abc_list$theta_star_vals)
  acc_rate  <- (acc_count / abc_list$total_sims) * 100
  y_stat_means <- colMeans(abc_list$Y_stat_vals)
  
  cat(sprintf("\n--- %s ---\n", model_name))
  cat("Accepted Count                 :", acc_count, sprintf("(Acceptance Rate: %.2f%%)\n", acc_rate))
  cat(sprintf("Observed Statistic (Mean, Med) : %.4f, %.4f\n", abc_list$X_stat_obs[1], abc_list$X_stat_obs[2]))
  cat(sprintf("Mean Simulated Stat (Y_bar,Med): %.4f, %.4f\n", y_stat_means[1], y_stat_means[2]))
  cat(sprintf("Mean Distance                  : %.4f\n", mean(abc_list$distances)))
  cat(sprintf("Max Distance (Must be < eps)  : %.4f\n", max(abc_list$distances)))
  cat("Estimated Posterior Mean (mu)  :", round(mean(abc_list$theta_star_vals), 4), "\n")
  cat("Estimated Posterior SD (mu)    :", round(sd(abc_list$theta_star_vals), 4), "\n")
}

cat("\n===================================================\n")
cat("            ABC FULL SIMULATION RESULTS            \n")
cat("===================================================\n")
cat("True Analytical Posterior Mean:", round(post_mean, 4), "\n")
cat("True Analytical Posterior SD  :", round(post_sd, 4), "\n")
cat("Epsilon Tolerance (epsilon)   :", epsilon, "\n")

# Print details for Choice 1
print_full_metrics(abc_euclidean, "1. STANDARD EUCLIDEAN DISTANCE")

# Print details for Choice 2
print_full_metrics(abc_weighted, "2. WEIGHTED EUCLIDEAN DISTANCE")

# Print details for Choice 3
print_full_metrics(abc_mahalanobis, "3. MAHALANOBIS DISTANCE")

cat("\n===================================================\n")
```
